$comment: The machine-readable half of section 7 of docs/security/credential-vault-threat-model.md. One entry per numbered rule there, with the same id. A `checked` rule is enforced by src/__tests__/structural/vault-boundaries.test.ts, which reads the Rust source as text on every `npm test`; a `prose-only` rule says why no text check can carry it. The test fails if this list and section 7 disagree, if a checked rule has no check, or if an anchor a check expects is missing (a check that finds nothing is broken, not green). Changing a name list here is a security decision: flag it for human review.

rules.title: Never return a decrypted field value from a #[tauri::command]
rules.reason: A decrypted value is a String once it leaves SecureString; no text pattern separates it from any other String a command returns.

rules.title: Never log plaintext, and never put it in an AppError message
rules.reason: Whether a formatted value is a secret is a data-flow question; SecureString's redacting Debug/Display is the structural guard, and rule 3 keeps its serialization closed.

rules.title: Never add Serialize to SecureString or EncryptedToken
A new secret-touching async command goes into PRIVILEGED_COMMANDS; an exclusion is recorded in the tier ledger
Never flip a fail-closed default in section 5
Every decrypt writes an audit row via audit_log, and must not block on that write
rules.reason: A decrypt path and its audit write can sit in different functions and crates; pairing them needs a call graph, not a text match. credential_audit_write_failures is the runtime signal.

rules.title: Do not widen execute_api_request's host; build_full_url is the single place that joins base URL and path
